memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: By the time Lot reached Zoar, the sun had risen over the land. Then the Lord rained down burning sulfur on Sodom and Gomorrah - from the Lord out of the heavens. Thus he overthrew those cities and the entire plain, destroying all those living in the cities - and also the vegetation in the land. - Gen 19:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The judgement falls. The moment Lot reaches safety, fire and burning sulphur rain down on Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities are utterly destroyed. This is a sobering, terrible scene, and Scripture does not soften it. God is holy, sin is deadly serious, and there comes a point when His patience gives way to justice.

We must hold this truth with reverence, not glee. God had been patient - remember, He would have spared the city for ten righteous people (Gen 18:32). He sent messengers, gave warnings, delayed until His servant was safe. But the wickedness was complete, the outcry of the victims was great, and justice finally came. God's patience is vast, but it is not endless.

This is not comfortable, but it is true, and we need it. A world that imagines God will never judge sin is a world deceived. The destruction of Sodom stands through all of Scripture as a solemn warning of real judgement to come (Jude 7; 2 Pet 2:6).

Yet even this drives us to the gospel. The same holy God who judged Sodom "did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all" (Rom 8:32). At the cross, the fire of God's judgement against sin fell - not on us, but on Jesus, who bore it in our place. The only safe refuge from the judgement to come is to be found in Christ. Flee to Him, and you will never face the fire.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you take the reality of God's judgement seriously?
- Have you fled to Christ, the only safe refuge from judgement?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Holy God, You are just, and sin is serious. Thank You that at the cross, the judgement I deserved fell on Jesus instead. Keep me safe in Him, my only refuge from the fire to come.
Amen.
